name: Museumsfriedhof Kramsach
kurzbeschreibung: The Kramsach Museum Cemetery ("Merry Cemetery"): a unique open-air museum for quirky, humorous grave inscriptions and wrought-iron art spanning five centuries.
beschreibung:
Overview

The world-famous Kramsach Museum Cemetery – affectionately known as the "Merry Cemetery" or "Cemetery without the Dead" – is located in the tranquil hamlet of Hagau in the Tyrolean municipality of Kramsach in the Kufstein district. This unique open-air museum is one of the most visited and original cultural-historical attractions in Western Austria. Over 900 artfully forged historical grave crosses and gravestones from across the Alpine region are gathered on an idyllic, tree-shaded meadow. They bear witness to an archaic, unspoiled folk culture that faced death not with fear, but with life-affirming, subtle, and sometimes crude humor.

Route & Requirements

The open-air museum was founded in 1965 through the initiative of Kramsach master blacksmith and stonemason Hans Guggenberger. Guggenberger recognized the invaluable cultural-historical value of the old hand-forged grave crosses, which were ending up in scrap heaps en masse during cemetery clearings in the Bavarian-Tyrolean and Salzburg regions. With great passion, he collected, de-rusted, and restored these wrought-iron artworks from five centuries (from the 17th to the early 20th century).

Visit & Arrival

The Kramsach Museum Cemetery is open daily year-round from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM (until 7:00 PM in summer). Admission to the open-air museum is free (voluntary donations at the entrance are requested for the preservation and ongoing maintenance of the valuable wrought-iron artworks). Arrival by car: Via the Inntal motorway A12, exit Kramsach/Alpbachtal, then follow directions towards Kramsach Zentrum and the signs for "Museumsfriedhof / Hagau" (large free parking lot available directly at the entrance Hagau 2). By public transport: Train (ÖBB) to Brixlegg station, from there take VVT bus line 4111 or 4074 every half hour directly to the Kramsach Museumsfriedhof stop. Arrival is straightforward and well-signposted, ensuring visitors can easily reach their destination.

Tips

The entire museum grounds are flat with well-maintained gravel and grass paths and are fully accessible for wheelchairs and strollers. Take your time strolling among the crosses to read the often small-print rhymes at your leisure and admire the detailed wrought-iron decorations. In the adjoining museum café and shop, visitors can purchase books with the collected sayings as original Tyrolean souvenirs. Comfortable footwear is recommended to fully enjoy the tour. The Museum Cemetery is a place of reflection and amusement, offering a unique perspective on life and death.
